name: Shimizu Robo-Welder
specialisedFor: on-site welding of steel column joints
summary: A column welding robot on a wheeled carriage that scans the weld groove with a laser and fills it automatically with a six-axis arm and MAG welding torch; usually two work as a pair on one steel column, on Shimizu's own sites.

germany.statusNote: Not sold: Shimizu developed Robo-Welder (with Osaka University) for its own steel-frame projects in Japan and plans to reuse each robot across its sites; no sale, rental or licence offer found.

specs.label: Arm payload
specs.conditions: maximum transport capacity of the arm (2018 spec)

specs.label: Arm reach
specs.conditions: maximum, 2018 spec table; a Shimizu diagram on the topic page shows 901 mm

specs.label: Groove sensor
specs.value: blue semiconductor laser, 405 nm, measuring range 200 mm ±48 mm

notes: Sits on a dedicated wheeled carriage that is guided to the column; from there it welds automatically without a worker.
One six-axis arm per robot (the English 2021 release says "six arms", the Japanese original says a six-axis arm); two robots usually weld one column from opposite sides.
Plans each weld from the laser-measured groove shape with a simulator developed with Osaka University.
Specifications are from 2018; the robot shown on site in 2021 looks different (blue arm instead of the orange arm in the 2018 photos), so values may have changed.

images.alt: Robo-Welder welding a steel column at the Toranomon-Azabudai site, shown with a weld layer drawing

evidence.task: Welded steel column joints with grooves of varying shape during trials
evidence.where: Robot laboratory, Shimizu Institute of Technology, Etchujima, Tokyo, Japan

evidence.task: Welded the 100 mm thick plates of the steel columns on the underground floors in 5 man-days per column instead of 8 for master welders; 14 robots planned for the above-ground floors to weld about 15% of around 1,800 km of welds
evidence.where: Toranomon-Azabudai Project, A district (64-storey tower), Minato-ku, Tokyo, Japan; Shimizu as contractor

openQuestions: Is Robo-Welder still in use on Shimizu sites after Toranomon-Azabudai, and how many robots exist?
Current specifications: the 2018 table and a Shimizu diagram disagree on arm reach (1,101 vs 901 mm) and arm weight (54 vs 52 kg).
